This apportionment for the successive years was as follows:⁵¹

1876-1877  $7.82          1882-1883  $3.25          1886-1887  $4.75
1877-1878  4.50           1883-1884  3.41           1887-1888  4.50

During the last four years of the College's operation, President Halbell's business acumen was able to turn to some account the Indian-school movement in Indian Territory and a change in the Government's policy of Indian Education. Unable to have Savoy College used as the desirable program for education of the Indian children in this Reservation, the Government of Indian Affairs during the early 'eighties had been trying various plans of subsidizing church schools in the East as well as in the Territory, not only for the schooling but for the feeding and schooling these Indian boys and girls. Some of his earlier letters and also some from his correspondence show the facilities and responsibility of the schools for the care of the pupils that no tuition institution could adequately offer. About 1884 or 1885, however, the Commissioner, perhaps in cooperation with the Secretary of the Interior, in his own use in Mr. Halbell a courageous and sagacious financial manager; he began to show in the writing the extent it Schools in the States might induce to attend.
